title: Quantification of Plant Hormones by Standard Addition Method
author: Takuyu Hashiguchi
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bqy6mxze
materials: Plant tissues of interest such as leaves, roots, and stems are disrupted in liquid nitrogen using a homogenizer (e.g. TissueLyzer II, QIAGEN).
Sonicate the solutions for 5 min at 4°C using a ultrasonicator (e.g. 1510J-MT, BRANSON) and then incubate on a tube rotator for 60 min at 4°C.

Prepare stock solutions by adding each plant hormone into one tube. When you make five working solutions, prepare five stock solutions (e.g. 0, 20, 200, 1000, 2000 ng/ml). In the case of a pre-spike method, you need to make those before adding to the matrix.
Analyze 10 μl of the sample by LC-MS/MS . In the present protocol, orbitrap Q-Exactive-linked to an UltiMate 3000RSLC (Thermo Fisher Scientific) is used.

Separate samples on a 2.6 μm Accucore C18 LC column (Thermo Fisher Scientific) using a linear methanol gradient of 1-100 % for 10 min at a flow rate of 0.5 ml/min. An autosampler and a column compartment are set at 10°C and 40°C, respectively.

steps.title: Extract Plant Tissue
steps.instruction: Collect 50 mg of tissue and extract with 1 ml of cold 50% acetonitrile. Prepare separate homogenized tissues for the sample and for each standard (e.g., six tissues total for one sample and five spiking solutions).

steps.title: Perform Pre-Spiking
steps.instruction: If using a pre-spike method, add pure standards to the tissue along with the 1 ml cold 50% acetonitrile.

steps.title: Centrifuge and Collect Supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the extract at 15,000 × g for 15 min and collect the supernatant into a new 2 ml tube.

steps.title: Activate and Equilibrate HLB Cartridge
steps.instruction: Prepare the Oasis HLB cartridge (Waters) through activation and equilibration.

substeps.instruction: Activate the cartridge with 1 ml of 100% methanol.
Wash with 1 ml of ultrapure water.
Equilibrate the cartridge with 1 ml of 50% acetonitrile.

steps.title: Load Sample and Collect Flow-through
steps.instruction: Load the collected supernatant onto the cartridge and collect the flow-through into a 15 ml tube.

steps.title: Elute and Evaporate Sample
steps.instruction: Elute the sample and concentrate it to dryness.

substeps.instruction: Elute with 1 ml of 30% acetonitrile into the tube.
Divide the eluate into two 2 ml tubes.
Evaporate to dryness in a vacuum concentrator (e.g. SPD140DDA, Thermo Fisher Scientific) for 3 hours or overnight.

steps.title: Reconstitute Dried Pellets
steps.instruction: Dissolve dried pellets in 100 μl of 30% acetonitrile, adjusting the volume as needed for dilution or concentration.

steps.title: Generate Matrix Calibration Curves
steps.instruction: Create calibration curves by diluting stock solutions with the matrix (e.g., add 2.5 μl of stock solution to 47.5 μl of matrix). Adjust dilution factors based on plant material or hormone concentration.

steps.title: Configure Mass Spectrometry
steps.instruction: Acquire MS data in targeted selected ion monitoring (t-SIM) mode using electrospray ionization (ESI).

substeps.instruction: Set polarity to both positive and negative ionization modes.
Set sheath gas flow rate to 50, auxiliary gas to 10, and sweep gas to 0.
Set heated capillary temperature to 380 °C and auxiliary gas heater temperature to 350 °C.
Set S-lens RF level to 50, resolution to 70,000, AGC target to 5E4, and maximum injection time to 200ms.
If monitoring a stable isotope, set isolation window at 10.0 m/z and offset at 2.0 m/z.

steps.title: Process and Analyze Data
steps.instruction: Use Xcalibur software to process raw data and quantify hormones.

substeps.instruction: Analyze raw data files using Qual Browser to verify target ion detection.
Analyze sequence files using Quan Browser to ensure correct peak extraction for target ions.
Subtract peak areas of standards from peak areas of the matrix to determine the calibration curve equation (y-intercept and slope).
Calculate plant hormone concentration by substituting the sample peak area into the equation.
